d1: close view of a steel cup adapter fitted on the head of a square wooden stake pressed into hard grass by a heavy grey SDS hammer drill, soil starting to jump around the stake
d2: the same stake sunk deep so the cup sits at ground level, loose soil and grass scattered around, the hammer drill still pressed down

A: the neighbour stands beside a row of short stakes in the grass with a five-kilo sledgehammer over his shoulder, sweaty, grumbling toward the presenter
K: the neighbour with the sledgehammer resting on his shoulder and a sceptical frown, one hand on his hip, the presenter beside a finished stake holding a heavy hammer drill
line: Yo con la maza tardé media hora en clavar cuatro.
text: Yo con la maza tardé media hora en clavar cuatro.

A: he lifts the heavy hammer drill, glances at a small stopwatch in his other hand and turns to the camera with a small calm smile
K: he holds the hammer drill hanging at his side and looks straight at the camera with a calm half smile, a driven stake behind him
text: Ocho segundos. Con un rotomartillo que alguien tiró a la basura.

d1: extreme close view of a steel pipe cup sitting on the head of a wooden stake, a hammer drill chisel shank welded on its flat top, the whole thing shaking hard from hammering
d2: the stake now much lower, cup pressed to the ground, dust and small clods flying

A: he stands in the workshop and kicks the pile of scrap pipes and plates beside him with his boot, talking to the camera
K: he stands with his boot on the scrap pile, one eyebrow raised, looking at the camera, the pile of pipes and plates shifted
text: Loco, ¿no? Un caño, una chapa y la cola de una mecha rota. Todo salió de esa pila.

A: the neighbour has his arms crossed now, shaking his head slowly, looking at the presenter with a sceptical half smile
K: the neighbour with crossed arms and tilted head, the presenter holding the hammer drill next to him, both beside the stakes
line: Eso se rompe a la primera, ya vas a ver.
text: Eso se rompe a la primera, ya vas a ver.

A: he holds up a cracked cup adapter in one hand and a split wooden stake in the other, looking at the camera with a rueful face
K: he holds the cracked adapter and the split stake side by side at chest height, looking at the camera, lips pressed
text: Y tenía razón. Se rompió. Dos veces. Y no fue por mala suerte.

A: he puts the split stake down on the workbench and points at it with a greasy finger, talking to the camera
K: he leans on the workbench with both hands, looking at the camera, the split stake and the adapter in front of him
text: Te voy a mostrar exactamente por qué, porque eso que falló es lo que casi nadie te cuenta.

A: he stands on a grass field beside a sagging old wire fence with rotten leaning stakes, gesturing along the line of the fence toward the far end
K: he points down the length of the sagging fence with his arm extended, looking at the camera
text: Todo empezó con un amigo, que tiene un campito con el alambrado tirado por la última tormenta.

A: he crouches at the base of a rotten stake and pulls it out of the soil easily with one hand, showing it
K: he holds up a rotten stake eaten at the base, looking at the camera with a sad shrug
text: Estacas podridas al ras, alambre en el pasto. Necesitaba cien estacas nuevas, en ciento veinte metros.

A: he swings a five-kilo sledgehammer down onto a stake head and it lands a little off centre, he winces
K: he leans on the sledgehammer handle breathing hard, looking down at a stake that is only a hand deep in the ground
text: Yo probé a maza, como todos. Con una maza de cinco kilos, la estaca se me clavó bien poquito.

A: he rubs the small of his back with one hand, looking at the row of stakes still to drive
K: he stands with a hand on his lower back looking at a long row of stakes lying in the grass, tired
text: Hice las cuentas: cien estacas, dos tardes enteras. Y la espalda hecha pedazos.

A: he holds a post-hole digger standing in the grass and shakes his head at it, looking at the camera
K: he stands with a post-hole digger planted in the grass, shaking his head at the camera with a wry face
text: Una hoyadora te hace el pozo, pero para estacas finas es matar una hormiga con un cañón: cien pozos, y encima hay que rellenar.

A: the neighbour leans on the old fence wire holding his sledgehammer, talking to the presenter with a lopsided smile
K: the neighbour leaning on a stake with the sledgehammer at his feet, arms folded over the top of it
line: Con la maza. Como toda la vida, sin inventos.
text: Con la maza. Como toda la vida, sin inventos.

A: he taps the top of a stake with his knuckles, looking at it thoughtfully, then looks up at the sky
K: he stands with a hand on his chin looking at a stake, deep in thought, sledgehammer lying in the grass
text: Y ahí se me ocurrió: un rotomartillo golpea mucho más fuerte que yo, y no se cansa. ¿Y si lo uso para clavar?

A: he shrugs and walks a few steps with the sledgehammer over his shoulder, turning back to the camera
K: he stands in the grass facing the camera, sledgehammer on his shoulder, chin raised in a half-smile
text: Sin girar, solo el golpe. Lo único que me faltaba era un rotomartillo. Y no tenía uno.

A: he crosses his arms and looks at the neighbour with a mischievous half smile, chin up
K: he stands with arms crossed facing the neighbour, a challenging half smile
text: Y se lo dije al vecino: si clavo una estaca en menos de un minuto, el asado del domingo lo pones tú.

A: the neighbour uncrosses his arms and puts out a big rough hand to shake, laughing
K: the neighbour with his hand held out over the fence wire, a big challenging grin
line: Trato hecho. Y si pierdes, la carne la pones tú y la leña también.
text: Trato hecho. Y si pierdes, la carne la pones tú y la leña también.

A: he shakes the neighbour's hand firmly and turns back to the camera, eyebrows raised
K: he holds the shaken hand up, looking at the camera with a raised eyebrow and a half smile
text: Ya no era solo por la espalda. Ahora había un asado en juego, y no pensaba perderlo.

A: he walks along a neighbourhood street beside a big yellow rubbish skip full of rubble, looking into it, talking to the camera
K: he stands at the edge of the skip leaning in, one hand on the rim, pointing at something inside it with the other
text: Justo esa semana, volviendo del taller, pasé al lado de una obra. Y en el volquete, entre los escombros, lo vi.

A: he pulls a dusty grey SDS-max hammer drill out of the rubble by its handle, cable trailing without a plug, and looks it over
K: he holds the dusty hammer drill up in both hands with its cable hanging cut, looking at it with a pleased frown
text: Un rotomartillo SDS-max, de los pesados. Sin ficha, con el cable pelado y lleno de polvo de cemento.

A: he presses the chisel end against his palm and rattles the tool next to his ear, listening
K: he holds the hammer drill next to his ear, eyes on the ground, listening carefully
text: Lo sacudí al lado de la oreja. Se oía entero por dentro. Nadie lo miraba, así que me lo llevé al hombro.

A: he walks away down the street with the heavy hammer drill on his shoulder, looking back at the camera with a mischievous smile
K: he stops in the street with the hammer drill on his shoulder and turns his head to the camera, grinning slightly
text: Ya sé lo que estás pensando: capaz que estaba roto. Por eso lo primero fue revisarlo.

A: he sits on the kerb next to the skip and turns the hammer drill over in his hands, looking at its worn end
K: he sits on the kerb with the hammer drill across his knees, looking at it, a small smile
text: Pesaba unos cinco kilos, de puro golpe. Nada de electrónica rara: un mecanismo simple y bruto.

A: he stands and sets off along the street with the tool on his shoulder, the skip behind him
K: he walks away with the hammer drill on his shoulder, looking back over it at the camera
text: De los que se arreglan con un destornillador. Justo lo que quería.

A: he sets the dusty hammer drill down on the wooden workbench of his workshop and wipes his hands on a rag, looking at it
K: he stands behind the workbench with the hammer drill in front of him, the rag over his shoulder, looking at the tool
text: Pero antes, el inventario. Lo que vas a necesitar es poco, y casi todo es chatarra.

d1: close view of a rusty piece of thick round steel pipe about seven centimetres wide lying on the wooden bench beside a tape measure
d2: the same pipe with a thumb pressing the tape measure to its open end, a chalk line on it
text: Un caño de setenta y seis milímetros de diámetro, de una cama vieja. Diez centímetros de largo te alcanzan.

d1: close view of a thick square plate of steel, rust on the edges, on the bench next to a caliper
d2: the same plate with the caliper closed over its edge showing the thickness
text: Una chapa de diez milímetros. La mía era la tapa de una alcantarilla que se había roto en la vereda.

d1: close view of a broken hammer drill bit lying on the bench, its long shank ending in a splintered end
d2: the same bit now held up between two fingers, the useful shank about ten centimetres long
text: Y la cola de una mecha SDS-max rota. No hace falta gastar una buena: con diez centímetros de vástago alcanza.

A: he stands with the three pieces lined up on the bench in front of him, tapping each with a finger, talking to the camera
K: he holds his arms open above the three pieces on the bench, shrugging with a half smile, looking at the camera
text: Eso es todo lo que lleva el hincapostes. Un caño, una chapa y una mecha rota. Gasto en materiales: cero.

A: he takes a length of wooden two-by-two stake from a bundle leaning on the wall and holds it toward the camera
K: he holds the wooden stake upright next to his face, tapping it, looking at the camera
text: Las estacas: eucalipto de dos por dos pulgadas, ochenta centímetros. Cuarenta van enterrados, cuarenta afuera.

A: he opens a cardboard box on the bench and takes out a few welding electrodes and a spare cutting disc, showing them
K: he holds three welding electrodes and a worn cutting disc in one hand, looking at the camera
text: Y de consumibles: tres electrodos, un disco de corte, y arena seca para más adelante.

A: he taps his chest with a greasy hand and shrugs with a proud half smile
K: he stands with his arms crossed and a proud half smile, looking at the camera, the scrap pile behind him
text: Lo que te va a costar de verdad: unos electrodos y un rato. El resto, lo tiran otros.

A: he stands in front of a scratched blackboard that has tool outlines chalked on it and taps it with a piece of chalk while talking
K: he holds the chalk against the blackboard, half turned to the camera, looking at it
text: Para que lo veas entero antes de empezar: son seis pasos. Uno, dejar el rotomartillo andando.

A: he draws a short line on the blackboard with the chalk, glancing at the camera
K: he holds the chalk near a drawn line on the blackboard, glancing at the camera
text: Dos, sacar el vástago de la mecha rota. Tres, cortar el caño. Cuatro, hacer la tapa con un agujero justo.

A: he taps the blackboard with the chalk, one step at a time, nodding
K: he stands with the chalk raised beside the board and a small smile, looking at the camera
text: Cinco, soldar todo. Y ahí está el error que me costó dos estacas. Y seis, preparar las estacas.

A: he puts the chalk down on the shelf and wipes his palms on his trousers, turning to the camera
K: he faces the camera with his greasy hands open at his sides, casual, half smile
text: Si te gustan estos inventos con chatarra, quédate en el taller, que hay más. Vamos a empezar.

A: he holds the hammer drill upside down on the bench and unscrews its rear cover with a screwdriver, looking at the inside
K: he lifts off the grey rear cover and looks into the tool at the carbon brushes, one thumb inside
text: Paso uno. Antes de enchufar nada, abro el rotomartillo y miro las escobillas de carbón.

d1: close view of two small worn carbon brushes held with tweezers over the open motor of a hammer drill, black dust on the grey housing
d2: the same two carbon brushes now blown clean and placed back in their holders, the housing wiped
text: Están gastadas, pero todavía sirven. Las soplo, limpio el polvo negro y las vuelvo a poner.

A: he strips the cut cable with a knife on the bench and screws a new plug on it, looking down at his hands
K: he presses the new black plug on the end of the cable with his thumb, looking down at it with a calm face
text: Al cable pelado le pongo una ficha nueva. Ojo con la conexión a tierra: cable verde y amarillo al pin del medio.

A: he squeezes grease from a small tube into the front of the hammer drill, looking down
K: he wipes the front of the hammer drill with a rag, looking down at it, a smear of grease on his thumb
text: Un poco de grasa en el frente, donde entra el vástago. Y ahora sí, a enchufarlo.

A: he puts on ear defenders and safety glasses in front of the camera, touching each in turn
K: he stands with ear defenders and safety glasses on, a thumb up toward the camera
text: Protección de oídos, anteojos, guantes. Esto hace un ruido que te deja sordo si no te proteges.

A: he plugs the hammer drill into a wall socket and lifts it, pointing the chisel end at the floor
K: he holds the hammer drill pointed at the floor with his finger near the switch and looks at the small mode dial on its side
text: Y acá viene lo más importante de todo el video: el selector de modo.

d1: close view of a thumb turning the mode dial of a grey SDS-max hammer drill from the drilling symbol to the chisel-only symbol
d2: the dial now clicked onto the chisel-only symbol, the thumb resting beside it
text: Tiene que quedar en el martillo solo, el del cincel. Sin rotación. Si gira, te tuerce la estaca y te tuerce la muñeca.

A: he presses the trigger and the hammer drill thumps against a thick plank on the floor, he looks at it with satisfaction
K: he holds the running hammer drill pointed at the plank with both hands, a faint grin, looking at it
text: Prueba en un tablón. Funciona. Percusión pura, y con ganas. Del volquete a mi taller, sin un peso.

A: he sets an opened-up hammer drill mechanism on the bench and points into it with a screwdriver, talking
K: he points with a screwdriver at the open mechanism of a hammer drill, looking at the camera
text: ¿Y por qué solo percusión? Porque adentro el rotomartillo tiene un pistón que empuja el aire.

A: he mimes a punch with his fist toward the camera, the open mechanism on the bench
K: he holds his fist forward like a punch, looking at the camera, the open mechanism on the bench
text: Ese aire empuja un percutor, y el percutor golpea la cola del cincel. Miles de golpes por minuto.

A: he holds the chisel end of the hammer drill toward the camera, shaking his head slightly
K: he holds the chisel end of the hammer drill toward the camera, a small serious frown
text: Esa energía es la que necesitamos. Pero no está hecho para clavar madera, y hay que dársela por la cola.

A: he gestures at the adapter parts on the bench with both hands
K: he gestures with both hands open toward the adapter parts on the bench, looking at the camera
text: Por eso el adaptador: la copa recibe el golpe del vástago y se lo pasa a la estaca sin romperla.

A: he sets a stake on the bench and lays a pipe ring on its top like a cap, pressing it down
K: he presses the pipe ring down onto the head of a stake on the bench, looking at the camera
text: Es como un dedal en la cabeza de la estaca. La copa la abraza, y el golpe baja derecho.

A: he clamps the broken drill bit in a vice on the workbench, wearing safety goggles, and marks a line with a marker
K: he holds a marker at a line on the bit clamped in the vice, looking down at it through safety goggles
text: Paso dos. Pongo la mecha rota en la morsa y marco diez centímetros de cola, contando desde la punta del vástago.

d1: close view of an angle grinder cutting the shank of a bit clamped in a vice, orange sparks flying to the right
d2: the same cut nearly through, a thin orange glow at the cut and a heavy spray of sparks
text: Amoladora, con anteojos puestos. Las chispas van derecho a los ojos, y un ojo no se compra en la ferretería.

A: he blows on the cut end of the shank and inspects it under the fluorescent light
K: he holds the short cut shank up to the light between two fingers, looking at its end with a frown
text: Esto es acero templado, muy duro. Acuérdate de este dato, porque más adelante me pasa factura.

A: he puts the cut shank into a small tin and shakes it, grinning at the camera
K: he holds a small tin with the cut shank inside, shaking it lightly, grinning
text: Y el resto de la mecha no se tira: lo guardo, que siempre sirve para un punzón o un pasador.

A: he clamps the thick steel pipe in the vice and marks a cut line ten centimetres from the end with a paint marker
K: he holds the marker at the pipe line, looking down at it, tongue pressed against his cheek
text: Paso tres. El caño. Mido diez centímetros, y marco todo alrededor con una hoja de papel enrollada como guía.

d1: close view of an angle grinder cutting through a rusty steel pipe clamped in a vice, sparks flying forward
d2: the pipe cut through, the ring falling into his glove, sparks dying out
text: Amoladora otra vez. Nunca apoyada: siempre entrando, con las dos manos, y las chispas lejos de las botellas.

A: he lays the cut pipe ring on a flat steel plate and checks it for squareness with a small square, frowning
K: he holds the small square against the cut pipe ring showing a thin gap of light on one side, looking at it with a frown
text: Me pasé, un milímetro torcido de un lado. Lo llevo al disco y lo escuadro, porque el golpe tiene que bajar parejo.

A: he files the sharp edge of the cut pipe on the bench, brushing off filings with his hand
K: he runs his thumb over the smoothed edge of the pipe ring, looking down at it, satisfied
text: Le saco el filo con la lima, que es la parte que va a abrazar la cabeza de la estaca.

A: he holds a hole saw core bit in one hand and the pipe ring in the other, comparing them, looking at the camera
K: he holds up a metal core bit and the pipe ring side by side, looking at the camera with an evaluating frown
text: Alguien me va a decir: usa una corona de perforar. Sirve, pero hay que gastar una buena. Un caño de chatarra no cuesta nada.

d1: close view of a caliper measuring the inside of the cut pipe ring, reading sixty-eight millimetres
d2: the same caliper measuring across the diagonal of a square stake head, reading seventy millimetres
text: Ojo con estos números. Por dentro el caño mide sesenta y ocho. La diagonal de una estaca de dos por dos, setenta.

A: he tries to press a square stake head into the pipe ring, it does not go in, he frowns at the camera
K: he holds the stake head against the pipe ring, showing it does not enter, looking at the camera with a wry smile
text: O sea que no entra. Todavía no lo sabía, pero ese centímetro me iba a dar dos problemas.

A: he lays a thin three-millimetre steel sheet on the bench and traces the pipe ring on it with a marker, talking
K: he lifts the pipe ring away from a traced circle on a thin sheet, looking at it, a slightly unsure face
text: Paso cuatro, la tapa. Y acá hice lo que hice la primera vez: agarré la chapa que tenía a mano. Fina, de tres milímetros.

d1: close view of an angle grinder cutting a rough circle out of a thin steel sheet, sparks flying
d2: the circle cut out, a rough round disc sitting on the bench beside the sheet
text: La corto, redonda. Me salió lindo, y fácil. Hasta ahí, un placer.

d1: close view of a hand drill making an eighteen millimetre hole in the centre of a steel disc, a thin curl of metal rising
d2: the hole done, a bright drilled edge, the shank end poking through it
text: Y el agujero de dieciocho milímetros en el medio, justo para que el vástago pase ajustado.

A: he pulls a welding helmet down at the workbench, the workshop dimming, and strikes an arc on a steel piece, blue glow on his face
K: he holds the electrode holder over a steel piece, welding helmet down, a blue-white arc at the tip
text: Paso cinco. Soldar. Careta bajada antes de encender el arco, siempre. La luz del arco te quema la vista.

A: he holds up a welding electrode toward the camera with the ground clamp visible on the bench
K: he holds a welding electrode up toward the camera, the ground clamp clipped on the bench behind it, looking at it
text: Electrodo de dos coma cinco, bien seco. Ropa de algodón o de cuero, nada sintético que se derrita, y con ventilación.

d1: close view of a welding electrode laying a bead around a short steel shank passing through a hole in a thin steel disc, bright blue-white arc, smoke
d2: the bead finished all around the shank, a dark slag crust glowing dull red
text: Le doy un cordón alrededor del vástago, por arriba y por abajo. Fuerte, o eso creía.

A: he lifts the helmet and taps the slag off the weld with a chipping hammer, looking closely at it
K: he holds the welded disc up to the fluorescent light, looking at the weld with his glasses pushed up
text: Le saco la escoria. Se ve bien, ¿no? Parece una soldadura de manual. Así me pareció a mí.

A: the neighbour appears at the open workshop door frame with a mug in his hand, peering in at the welding bench
K: the neighbour leaning on the doorframe with his mug, the presenter at the bench with the welded disc in his hands
line: ¿Y eso qué es? ¿Un sombrero para las estacas?
text: ¿Y eso qué es? ¿Un sombrero para las estacas?

A: he looks at the neighbour over his glasses with a dry look, holding up the disc
K: he lowers the disc and looks toward the doorway with a dry half smile
text: Un sombrero, sí. Un sombrero de acero para estacas. Pasa y mira, pero con anteojos.

A: he places the disc on the pipe ring and tacks it in three points, helmet down
K: he holds the assembled steel cup adapter in both hands, turning it slowly, looking at it with a pleased face
text: Uno el disco al caño con tres puntos, y ahí está: mi primer hincapostes. Vamos a probarlo.

A: he cuts a long eucalyptus board into stake lengths with a handsaw on a sawhorse in the yard, sawdust flying
K: he saws through an eighty-centimetre stake with the handsaw on the sawhorse, looking down at the cut
text: Paso seis, las estacas. Las corto de ochenta, con serrucho, en el caballete. Cuarenta van enterrados.

A: he compares two wooden stakes, one dense eucalyptus and one soft pine, tapping them together, looking at the camera
K: he holds a dense eucalyptus stake and a soft pine stake side by side toward the camera
text: Un consejo con la madera: eucalipto, o algo duro. Con pino blando, la cabeza se aplasta antes de entrar.

A: he stands a stake on a chopping block and sharpens one end to a wedge point with a hatchet, chips flying
K: he holds the stake with a freshly cut wedge point up to the light, looking at it
text: Le hago punta en cuña con el hacha, así entra en la tierra sin trabarse.

d1: close view of a blowtorch flame charring the pointed end of a wooden stake, thin smoke and black crust forming
d2: the same stake end fully charred black and glossy, the flame moving away
text: Y quemo con el soplete la parte que va bajo tierra. Carbonizada, la madera se pudre más despacio.

A: he carries a bundle of stakes over his shoulder to the grass and looks at the camera with a doubtful smile
K: he stands with a bundle of stakes on his shoulder, looking at the camera with a doubtful smile
text: Y ya están las estacas listas, con las esquinas todavía sin biselar. ¿Ves por dónde va la cosa?

A: he stands in the grass with the hammer drill fitted with the new adapter, ear defenders around his neck, looking at a stake standing in the soil
K: he fits the cup over the head of a square stake standing in the grass, holding the hammer drill with both hands, looking at the stake
text: Estaca de dos por dos, tierra del patio, la misma de todo el video. Le apoyo la copa encima, aunque no baja del todo.

A: he pulls the ear defenders and safety glasses on, checks his stance and squeezes the trigger, hammering on the stake
K: he leans on the running hammer drill pressing the cup on the stake, teeth clenched, the stake vibrating
text: Anteojos, protección de oídos, guantes de cuero. Y nunca, nunca la mano cerca de la estaca.

A: the neighbour steps closer with his arms crossed, grinning with mocking eyes at the presenter
K: the neighbour with crossed arms and a smug grin, the presenter looking down at something in the grass, the hammer drill on the ground
text: ¡Eh! ¿Y eso? Se rajó.

A: he picks up the split stake and holds it in the light, looking at its head crushed and cracked down the middle, frowning
K: he holds the stake with its head split in two along the grain, looking at it with a grim little frown
text: Se partió al medio, por la veta. La estaca número uno, para la leña.

d1: close view of the cup adapter lying on the grass with its thin lid dented like a soft tin can and a hairline crack in the weld around the shank
d2: the same view a moment later, a hand lifting the adapter, the crack in the weld now open

A: he lifts the cracked adapter and shows it to the camera with a resigned look, the neighbour laughing softly out of frame
K: he holds up the dented adapter beside his face and looks at the camera, pressing his lips together
text: Y la tapa, abollada como una lata. Y la soldadura, agrietada. Dos golpes, y todo el trabajo al suelo.

A: the neighbour claps a hand on the presenter's shoulder, shaking his head kindly but amused
K: the neighbour with a hand on the presenter's shoulder, both looking at the cracked adapter in the grass
line: Ya te lo dije. Con la maza no falla.
text: Ya te lo dije. Con la maza no falla.

A: he pats the neighbour's hand off his shoulder with a tired smile and picks up the adapter, thinking
K: he stands with the cracked adapter in one hand, looking at it thoughtfully, chin down
text: Tenía razón esta vez. Pero yo quería saber por qué. Porque una cosa rota siempre dice por qué se rompió.

A: he sets the cracked adapter down on the bench under the fluorescent tube and leans over it with his hands flat on the wood
K: he leans over the bench looking at the cracked adapter, both hands flat, thinking hard
text: Dos problemas, y los dos tienen explicación. Primero, la tapa.

d1: close view of a thin three-millimetre steel lid on a pipe ring, a thumb pressing the dent in its centre
d2: the same lid seen from the side, showing how much it has bowed inward
text: Tres milímetros es poco. La tapa se dobla como una cuchara, y el golpe no baja parejo, se queda en el centro.

d1: close view of a wooden stake head in the palm of a hand, its sharp corners chipped and splintered along the grain
d2: the same head turned, a long crack visible running down the side of the wood
text: Segundo, las cuatro esquinas de la estaca. Son la parte más débil de la madera, y ahí se abre la veta.

A: he pushes the broken stake head against the inner wall of the pipe ring showing it does not fit evenly, looking at it
K: he holds the pipe ring with the broken stake head jammed diagonally in it, looking at the gap on one side
text: La estaca entra torcida, el golpe va de costado, y la madera se abre. Lo que la copa tiene que hacer es abrazarla.

d1: close view of a caliper across the diagonal of a square stake head reading seventy millimetres, then across the inside of a pipe ring reading sixty-eight
d2: the same stake head with its corners planed, the caliper reading sixty across the diagonal
text: La cuenta era esta: setenta de diagonal, sesenta y ocho de hueco. No entra. Con las esquinas biseladas, sesenta. Entra justo.

A: he taps the hardened steel shank on the bench with a small hammer and shows the crack at the weld, looking at the camera
K: he holds the cracked shank and disc in his open palm toward the camera with a knowing look
text: Y la soldadura. Te dije que la mecha es acero templado, y el acero templado no se suelda en frío.

A: he shrugs and shakes his head with a small laugh, tapping his temple
K: he stands with his arms open in a small shrug, looking at the camera with an amused face
text: Soldar acero templado sin precalentar es como pegar un vidrio con cinta: al primer golpe, se abre.

A: he takes off his cap and rubs his curly hair, looking at the scrap pile
K: he stands with his cap in one hand and looks at the scrap pile with narrowed eyes, thinking
text: Y ahí entendí que me faltaban tres cosas: chapa más gruesa, precalentar, y un poco de oficio con la estaca.

A: he lays a thick ten millimetre steel plate on the bench and traces the pipe ring on it with a marker
K: he lifts the pipe ring away from a traced circle on a thick steel plate, nodding to himself
text: La chapa de diez milímetros, la de la alcantarilla. Otra vez a marcar, y otra vez a cortar.

d1: close view of an angle grinder cutting a round disc out of a thick steel plate, a heavy spray of orange sparks
d2: the thick disc cut out, glowing dull orange at the edge, smoke rising
text: Con esta el disco sufre. Paciencia, sin apurar, que se gasta un disco entero.

d1: close view of a hand drill boring an eighteen millimetre hole in the centre of a thick steel disc with a bit of oil on it, curls of metal rising
d2: the finished hole, bright and clean, oil shining around it
text: Agujero de dieciocho, despacio y con un poco de aceite, para no quemar la broca.

A: he holds the short hardened shank with pliers over a small torch and heats it, the tip glowing dull red
K: he holds the glowing dull-red shank in pliers over a bucket of sand, looking at it closely through his safety glasses
text: Y ahora lo que me faltaba: precalentar la cola de la mecha, hasta que se ponga rojo oscuro.

A: he buries the glowing shank in a bucket of dry sand and looks at the camera
K: he holds a scoop of sand over the shank buried in the bucket, looking at the camera, calm
text: Y a enfriar lento, tapada con arena seca. Nada de agua: el agua la vuelve a endurecer y vuelve a romper.

A: he pulls his welding helmet down and welds the shank into the thick disc on the bench, the arc lighting his face blue
K: he holds the electrode holder with his helmet down over the shank passing through the thick disc, bright blue-white arc, smoke
text: Ahora sí: electrodo básico, dos pasadas, por los dos lados del disco. Sin apurarme.

A: he hits the finished weld hard several times with a hammer and listens, then shows it to the camera
K: he holds the disc with its shank toward the camera after hammering, the weld intact, nodding
text: La prueba del martillazo: le doy unos golpes fuertes a la soldadura. Si suena limpio y no salta nada, sirve.

A: he lifts the helmet and chips slag off the finished weld with a small hammer, looking closely
K: he holds the finished disc with the shank up to the light, the weld a neat even bead, looking at it with a pleased face
text: Un cordón parejo, sin poros. Y no lo pulo: lo dejo como salió, que cuanto más grueso, mejor.

A: he presses the finished cup onto a chamfered stake on the bench and wiggles it to test the fit
K: he lifts the cup with the stake hanging inside it by friction, smiling at the camera
text: Y pruebo el encaje en seco. Entra justo, con un poco de juego. La estaca cuelga sola, sin caerse.

A: he clamps a wooden stake in the vice and planes its four corners with a hand plane at forty-five degrees, wood shavings curling
K: he holds the planed stake head up to the light, four bright chamfers visible on its corners, looking at it
text: Y ahora el truco de las estacas: le biselo las cuatro esquinas de la cabeza, a cuarenta y cinco grados.

d1: close view of a wooden stake head with four planed chamfers being slid into a steel pipe ring, a snug fit
d2: the same head fully seated, a small even gap around it
text: Así entra derecha, sin trabarse, y la madera no se abre, porque el caño la abraza de todos lados.

A: he welds the thick disc onto the pipe ring on the bench, helmet down, sparks on the bench
K: he lifts the helmet, holding the finished adapter, a fat weld ring visible around its top, looking at it
text: Uno el disco al caño con un cordón alrededor. Y el hincapostes está terminado. Otra vez, a probar.

A: he stands in the grass in front of a fresh stake, safety glasses and ear defenders on, the adapter fitted on his hammer drill, the neighbour beside him with a stopwatch in hand
K: he stands with the adapter on the stake head and both hands on the hammer drill, looking down at it, calm
text: Segunda vuelta. Estaca nueva, con las cuatro esquinas biseladas, y el vecino ahora con el cronómetro.

A: the neighbour holds up a small stopwatch, thumb on the button, looking at the presenter with narrowed eyes
K: the neighbour lowering the stopwatch with his thumb still on it, eyebrows raised
line: A ver, a ver. Yo te tomo el tiempo.
text: A ver, a ver. Yo te tomo el tiempo.

A: he takes a slow breath and looks at the stake, one hand raising three fingers
K: he holds up three fingers slowly with the hammer drill in the other hand, looking at the camera, tense
text: Respiro. Tres, dos, uno.

A: he braces his legs wide and squeezes the hammer drill trigger with the cup pressed on the stake, dust and soil rising
K: he leans his weight on the hammering hammer drill, the stake half sunk, looking down at it with a calm concentrated face
text: Sin empujar de más. El peso del rotomartillo hace el trabajo, yo solo lo dirijo. Y ahí va.

d1: close view of the cup adapter riding down over a wooden stake as it sinks in the soil, soil jumping around it, the tool shaking
d2: the stake sunk to the ground, the cup pressed against the grass, the hammering stopping, a puff of dust

A: he lifts the hammer drill off the sunk stake and looks at the neighbour, breathing out
K: he lifts the hammer drill away from a stake sunk deep in the ground, looking at the neighbour with a half smile
text: Ocho segundos. Cuarenta centímetros de estaca adentro, y sin una sola grieta.

A: the neighbour looks at the stopwatch, then at the stake, scratching his cap, mouth open a little
K: the neighbour looking at the stopwatch in his palm with his cap pushed back, stunned
line: Ocho… no puede ser. Bueno. Otra vez, que no te creo.
text: Ocho… no puede ser. Bueno. Otra vez, que no te creo.

A: he moves to a second stake and drives it in again, the neighbour crouching beside him holding the stopwatch
K: he lifts the hammer drill from the second sunk stake, the neighbour holding up the stopwatch to show the camera
text: Segunda estaca: nueve segundos. La tercera, ocho. La cuarta, siete y medio, cuando agarras el ritmo.

A: he pulls the adapter off a driven stake and checks the lid and the weld with his thumb, looking closely
K: he holds the adapter up to the light showing the thick lid and weld intact, looking at it with a smile
text: Miro la tapa, miro la soldadura. Intactas. Ahora sí, eso es un hincapostes.

A: he sets a spirit level against a stake standing in the grass and checks that it is vertical, looking at the bubble
K: he holds the spirit level against a stake, bending to look at the bubble, calm
text: Un truco de oficio: primero el nivel. La estaca tiene que estar recta antes del primer golpe, porque después no la enderezas.

A: he pulses the trigger briefly so the hammer drill taps the stake and the stake seats itself in the soil
K: he holds the hammer drill on the stake with light pressure, the stake seated a few centimetres, looking down at it
text: Los primeros golpes, cortitos, para que la estaca agarre. Recién ahí, gatillo a fondo.

A: he stands with legs apart and elbows against his body, the hammer drill vertical over a stake
K: he stands solidly with the hammer drill vertical over the stake, elbows tucked, looking at the top
text: Los pies separados, los codos pegados al cuerpo, y el rotomartillo bien vertical. Que el peso vaya derecho.

A: he lifts the hammer drill off and the cup stays stuck on the stake, he taps it loose and tilts it to look inside
K: he holds the cup adapter upside down looking at the inside, checking for wear
text: Al terminar, a veces la copa queda pegada por la vibración. Un golpecito, y sale.

A: he pushes a stake sideways with both hands to test how firm it is in the ground
K: he holds the top of a driven stake with both hands, shaking it to test it, looking at the camera with a satisfied nod
text: Y pruebo si aguanta, empujándola para los costados. Firme, como si la hubiera clavado un tractor.

A: he hands the sledgehammer to the neighbour and points at a fresh stake, smiling
K: the presenter holds out the sledgehammer and the neighbour takes it with a doubtful frown
text: Ahora tú con la maza. La misma estaca, el mismo suelo, y yo con el cronómetro.

A: the neighbour swings the sledgehammer down on a stake head, grunting, the stake going in a little
K: the neighbour leaning on the sledgehammer breathing hard, wiping his forehead with his forearm, the stake barely sunk
text: Ya… ya… ya casi.

A: he looks at the stopwatch in his hand and turns to the camera, shaking his head slightly with respect
K: he holds up the stopwatch toward the camera showing the numbers, looking at the neighbour with a small smile
text: Tres minutos y medio con la maza. Contra ocho segundos con el hincapostes. Sin trampa, en el mismo suelo.

A: he fits the cup on an unchamfered stake on purpose and hammers a short burst, the stake head splitting
K: he lifts the hammer drill off a stake whose head has split open along the grain, looking at the camera with a shrug
text: Y para que no me creas solo a mí: le puse una estaca sin biselar, a propósito. Mira cómo se abre.

A: he holds the split stake next to a clean chamfered one, looking at the camera
K: he holds the split stake and the clean chamfered stake side by side, looking at the camera, nodding
text: Misma copa, misma tierra, mismo rotomartillo. La única diferencia son cuatro biseles de un minuto de trabajo.

A: he kneels beside the stakes and pats the ground with his palm, talking to the camera
K: he crouches next to a driven stake pressing the soil beside it with his hand, looking at the camera, serious
text: Ahora la parte honesta. Esto anda en tierra blanda, de patio o de campo, y sin piedras.

A: he digs a stone out of the soil with a screwdriver and looks at the camera
K: he holds a stone dug out of the soil in his palm and shows it to the camera, shaking his head
text: Si hay una piedra, la estaca rebota. Y en tierra seca y dura, moja el suelo antes: sin agua, me tardó veinte segundos.

A: he holds a small notebook with a pencil and writes numbers, looking at the camera
K: he holds up a small notebook with a column of scribbled numbers toward the camera, tapping it with the pencil
text: Anoté diez estacas seguidas: entre siete y diez segundos cada una. Cien estacas son unos quince minutos de golpe puro.

A: he shrugs, looking at the camera, and spreads his hands
K: he stands with both hands open, shrugging, looking at the camera, honest face
text: Después está mover el alargue, medir cada metro veinte, y descansar. Por eso me llevó una mañana, no quince minutos.

A: he holds up the plug end of the cable with a thumb, pointing to the long extension cord curling across the grass
K: he stands holding the coil of a long orange extension cord, looking at the camera, one eyebrow raised
text: Necesitas corriente. Yo usé un alargue de treinta metros. Más lejos, un generador. Y es un límite real, no te lo escondo.

A: he points at the ground with the toe of his boot and looks back at the camera, serious
K: he stands over a stake with one boot beside a small patch of disturbed soil, looking at the camera with a serious face
text: Y antes de clavar, fíjate por dónde pasan los caños y los cables enterrados. Una estaca no ve nada.

A: he holds up a thick round post next to a thin stake, shaking his head, looking at the camera
K: he stands holding a thick round post and a thin stake side by side, looking at the camera with a small shrug
text: ¿Y para postes gruesos? No. Este funciona para estacas de dos por dos. Para un poste de cuatro pulgadas, no lo probé.

A: he walks along the row of stakes at the far end of the field with the hammer drill on his shoulder, the neighbour walking beside him carrying a coil of wire
K: he stops beside a long row of driven stakes with the coil-carrying neighbour beside him, looking along the fence line
text: Al final, las cien estacas no me llevaron dos tardes. Me llevaron una mañana.

A: he puts the hammer drill on the grass and rests the back of his hand on its housing, checking its temperature
K: he holds the back of his hand against the hammer drill housing, his face frowning, looking at it
text: Con una pausa cada diez estacas, porque el rotomartillo se calienta, y hay que dejarlo respirar.

A: he pulls out a stake that was driven crooked and re-drives it, looking at the base with a frown
K: he stands beside a re-driven stake pressing it straight with his palm, looking at it with a slight frown
text: A la número sesenta y dos apareció una piedra, y rebotó. La saqué con la barreta y seguí.

A: he points at a thick corner post set by hand at the end of the fence with a shovel leaning on it
K: he stands beside a thick corner post with a shovel leaning on it, looking at the camera
text: Los esquineros, en cambio, siguen yendo a pala: van más gruesos y más hondos, y esos no los clava esto.

A: the neighbour sits on a stake bucket with a mug in one hand and a sledgehammer on the grass, smiling and looking at the presenter
K: the neighbour with the mug raised in a salute toward the presenter, smiling under his cap
line: Bueno. Me callo. Pero me lo prestas el sábado.
text: Bueno. Me callo. Pero me lo prestas el sábado.

A: he looks at the neighbour and raises an eyebrow, pointing at him
K: he points at the neighbour with a raised eyebrow and a half smile
text: Un momento: ¿y el asado de la apuesta?

A: the neighbour groans, lifting his palms in surrender, laughing
K: the neighbour with both palms raised in surrender, laughing under his cap
line: Está bien, está bien. El domingo. La carne la pongo yo.
text: Está bien, está bien. El domingo. La carne la pongo yo.

A: he leans against a fence post and looks along the finished line, then at the camera
K: he leans on a fence post beside the finished stakes, looking at the camera with a satisfied smile
text: Lo que me gastó de verdad: dos electrodos, un disco y la mitad de un domingo. Lo demás, del volquete.

A: he laughs and shakes his head, looking at the camera, one hand on the hammer drill
K: he stands beside the finished fence line, looking at the camera with a warm relaxed smile
text: Y hay una última cosa que no te conté.

A: he holds a small pipe ring adapter over a thin steel rod pressed into vegetable garden soil, tapping it
K: he holds a small adapter over the head of a steel rod standing in the vegetable garden, looking at the camera
text: Con un caño más chico, el mismo vástago y la misma idea, clavo varillas para los tutores de los tomates.

A: he counts on his fingers, looking at the camera
K: he holds up four fingers toward the camera, serious but warm
text: Resumen de seguridad: anteojos, protección de oídos, guantes, y el rotomartillo siempre en martillo solo. Con eso te cuidas.

A: he holds up the three parts of the fix one by one, the thick disc, the planed stake and the sand bucket, looking at the camera
K: he stands holding the thick disc in one hand and a planed stake in the other, nodding at the camera
text: Y lo que aprendí a los golpes: chapa gruesa, precalentar la soldadura, y biselar las esquinas de la estaca. Tres cosas.

A: he stands in front of the camera with the sun low behind the fence, the hammer drill resting in the grass beside him
K: he looks straight into the camera with a friendly half smile, arms relaxed
text: Si tienes un rotomartillo viejo, no lo tires. Cuéntame qué harías tú con él, y lo pensamos juntos en los comentarios.

A: he points off to the side with his thumb toward the workshop as he talks to the camera
K: he holds his thumb pointing over his shoulder toward the workshop, smiling at the camera, ending
text: En el próximo, doblo un caño en un círculo perfecto con la chatarra que me sobró. Nos vemos en el taller.
